cases.title: Signed-out visitor verifies the static workflow preview against the exported JSON
preconditions: Visitor is signed out.
The landing route / is available.
setup: Open / at a desktop viewport.
steps: Read the graph nodes and edges and compare their displayed identifiers with the read-only exported workflow JSON.
Inspect representative graph node and edge labels without activating them.
Continue to the workflow export panel and compare the canonical identifiers.
assertions: Every graph node and edge displayed to the visitor has a matching identifier in the exported workflow JSON.
The static graph exposes no dialog, inspector, or activation semantics.
Every displayed node and edge retains a matching identifier in the canonical workflow JSON.

cases.title: Visitor selects the canonical workflow JSON without granting clipboard authority
preconditions: Visitor is signed out.
The landing route / is available.
setup: Open / and locate the graph workflow export panel.
steps: Activate the WorkflowSpec JSON selection action.
assertions: The read-only workflow JSON textarea receives focus and its entire value is selected.
A polite live-status message announces that the selection is ready.
The visitor can copy or inspect the complete workflow specification through normal browser controls without the page writing to the clipboard or requesting an artifact capability.

cases.title: Visitor can use the graph workflow without horizontal clipping across supported narrow viewports
preconditions: Visitor is signed out.
The landing route / is available.
setup: Test desktop 1440x960, mobile portrait 320x568 with reduced motion, tablet 768x1024, and mobile landscape 568x320 viewports.
steps: Navigate to the graph preview at each viewport.
On mobile, inspect the final static graph label and verify it remains inside the graph bounds.
In landscape, scroll to the workflow export panel.
assertions: The scroll area, preview, and graph fit the visible viewport and graph edges do not overlap nodes.
The static graph remains presentational at narrow widths and exposes no focusable node or edge controls.
At every tested viewport, the visitor can see the graph workflow and its export panel without horizontal clipping.

cases.title: Visitor navigates from the product navigation to each named landing section
preconditions: The landing route / is available.
setup: Open / at a viewport where the header navigation is available.
steps: Activate Why, Human control, and Open source from the product navigation.
assertions: Why targets the section with id why, Human control targets decision-workspace, and Open source targets open-source.
The visitor arrives at the named content section they selected.

cases.title: Signed-out visitor reaches account creation and sign-in routes from landing calls to action
preconditions: Visitor is signed out.
The landing route / is available.
setup: Open / and locate the graph, presentation, and final calls to action.
steps: Follow each Create account link.
Follow the final Sign in link.
assertions: Every Create account call to action targets /signup and the Sign in call to action targets /login.
The visitor is taken to the requested account-entry destination.

cases.title: Visitor opens the locale-appropriate presentation sample from landing
preconditions: The landing route / is available.
Inference: the presentation-sample navigation helper preserves the link destination for supported activation methods; its implementation is outside the sealed evidence.
setup: Open / in Korean and in a non-Korean locale.
steps: Activate the presentation sample link using mouse and keyboard without modifier keys.
Activate it with a modifier key to preserve normal link behavior.
assertions: The rendered sample href uses /demo/presentation?locale=ko for Korean and /demo/presentation?locale=en otherwise.
Inference: each supported activation reaches that locale's presentation sample in the browsing context selected by the navigation helper or native link behavior.
The visitor reaches the presentation sample corresponding to the locale shown on landing.

cases.title: Visitor can open the published SceneBoard source repository from landing
preconditions: The landing route / is available.
setup: Open / and locate the Open source section.
steps: Activate the View GitHub link from the Open source section.
assertions: The link targets https://github.com/leecatinc/sceneboard and declares a new browsing context.
The visitor is offered the public SceneBoard repository in a separate tab.

cases.title: Anonymous user signs in with valid email and password
preconditions: The initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
setup: Provide credentials accepted by the login session client.
steps: Open /login and wait for reconciliation to finish.
Enter a syntactically valid email and password.
Submit the sign-in form.
assertions: The email and password inputs expose their visible labels and are enabled only after reconciliation completes.
The primary action shows the signing-in state while the request is pending.
The browser navigates to /settings/ai-connections after a successful login, giving the user the configured post-login destination.

cases.title: Existing session bypasses the credential form
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with a non-null session snapshot.
steps: Open /login.
assertions: The browser navigates to /settings/ai-connections instead of offering a second sign-in flow.

cases.title: Credentials cannot be submitted before session reconciliation establishes the state
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation is pending.
steps: Open /login while reconciliation remains pending.
Attempt to focus or activate the credential and Google sign-in controls.
Resolve reconciliation with no session.
assertions: All sign-in controls are disabled while the session state is unknown, so a user cannot start a competing authentication attempt.
After reconciliation reports no session, the form becomes available for sign-in.

cases.title: Browser validation blocks empty or malformed credential submissions
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
steps: Leave a required credential empty, then attempt sign-in.
Enter a malformed email address, then attempt sign-in.
assertions: The browser keeps the user on /login and does not submit invalid credential input.
The user can correct the required email and password fields before an authentication request is started.

cases.title: Invalid credentials produce an accessible error and allow a corrected retry
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
setup: Make the first credential attempt return invalid_credentials and the corrected attempt succeed.
steps: Submit validly formatted but incorrect credentials.
Observe the error, correct the credentials, and submit again.
assertions: The invalid-credentials message is announced through the page alert and the controls become usable again.
The corrected retry reaches /settings/ai-connections, rather than leaving the user trapped after an authentication error.

cases.title: Unexpected credential login failure is recoverable without exposing a false success state
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
setup: Make the credential login result any handled non-success value other than invalid_credentials.
steps: Submit validly formatted credentials.
Observe the failure state and attempt a later retry after the service recovers.
assertions: The page shows the generic login-failed alert and does not navigate to the authenticated destination on failure.
The controls are re-enabled so the user can retry; a later successful retry reaches /settings/ai-connections.

cases.title: Google sign-in success reaches the same authenticated destination
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
The Google token acquisition resolves and the Google login result is successful.
steps: Open /login and activate Sign in with Google.
assertions: The Google action is unavailable while sign-in is in progress, preventing a second UI activation during the pending attempt.
After successful Google login, the browser navigates to /settings/ai-connections.

cases.title: Google invalid-credential response remains on login with a distinct accessible error
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
Google token acquisition resolves but the Google login result is invalid_credentials.
steps: Activate Sign in with Google.
assertions: The page remains on /login and announces the Google invalid-credentials message through the alert.
The sign-in controls are enabled again, allowing the user to choose a recovery action.

cases.title: Google provider cancellation or non-credential failure is recoverable
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation resolves with no session.
setup: Exercise both a rejected Google token acquisition and a handled non-success Google login result other than invalid_credentials.
steps: Activate Sign in with Google for each failure condition.
After either failure, complete a later successful Google or credential login.
assertions: Each failure announces the generic Google-failed alert and does not navigate to the authenticated destination.
The controls recover after each failure, and the later successful sign-in reaches /settings/ai-connections.

cases.title: Unsupported browser state is announced without enabling authentication controls
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation returns unsupported_browser.
steps: Open /login.
assertions: The page announces the unsupported-browser message through its alert.
Credential and Google sign-in controls remain disabled, leaving the user with a clear blocked state rather than a usable but unsafe form.

cases.title: Reconciliation-required state presents verification help and blocks new sign-in
preconditions: Initial session reconciliation returns reconciliation_required.
steps: Open /login.
assertions: The page announces verification-help text through its alert.
Credential and Google sign-in controls remain disabled, so the user does not proceed while session reconciliation is required.

cases.title: Concurrent renewal callers share the successful session recovery
preconditions: A reconciled session exists with a current generation.
Two callers request session renewal concurrently.
setup: Use the existing SessionRequestCoordinator renewal test fixture with two concurrent renewSession calls.
steps: Start both renewal calls before either completes.
assertions: Both callers receive an ok result backed by the renewed session snapshot.
The test fixture observes one renewal POST under one exclusive acquisition sequence.
[Inference] A user with concurrent in-app work can remain signed in after renewal instead of receiving divergent login recovery states.

cases.title: Generation drift or lost renewal response blocks stale authenticated work and requires recovery
preconditions: A session generation has been reconciled and an application request or renewal attempt is bound to it.
setup: Exercise generation drift before a shared dispatch and exercise renewal response loss after its intent is recorded.
steps: Attempt the bound dispatch after the generation changes.
Attempt a following request after the renewal response is lost.
assertions: Each attempt returns reconciliation_required rather than continuing the stale request; the drifted dispatch makes no additional network request.
[Inference] The caller can show its existing reconciliation-required recovery state instead of presenting data or success under an uncertain session.

cases.title: Public visitor sees loading followed by the shared board when bootstrap is ready
preconditions: A valid public share token returns a ready public-share state with at least one document page.
setup: Open /s/[shareToken] with the bootstrap action available.
steps: Observe the initial public-share screen.
Allow the ready bootstrap result to resolve.
assertions: A loading state is exposed while the share is initializing.
The visitor ultimately sees the shared board reader and its published title instead of an unavailable or password screen.

cases.title: Password-protected share denies empty and invalid admission without exposing board content
preconditions: The public share bootstrap returns password-required with a CSRF token.
setup: Open /s/[shareToken] as an unauthenticated public visitor.
steps: Attempt to submit the password form while its password field is empty.
Enter an invalid password and submit when the admission action returns password-invalid.
assertions: The empty-password submission control remains unavailable to the visitor.
An invalid-password alert is visible and focus remains on the password-entry path.
The protected board reader and artifact content are not shown after failed admission.

cases.title: Password admission rate limiting gives a clear denied-access outcome
preconditions: The password admission action returns rate-limited with retryAfterSeconds.
setup: Open a password-protected public share and submit a password request.
steps: Return the rate-limited admission state.
assertions: The visitor sees the rate-limited heading and the supplied retry delay.
Keyboard focus moves to the rate-limited message rather than leaving the visitor in the dismissed password form.
No protected board content becomes visible.

cases.title: Retryable revalidation preserves the visible board and recovers after Retry-After
preconditions: The visitor has a ready public-share state.
The first share-context revalidation returns a retryable response with Retry-After and the next response is ready.
setup: Open the board and advance past the 30-second early refresh boundary.
steps: Deliver the retryable revalidation response.
Advance by its retry delay and deliver the next ready response.
assertions: The already visible published board remains readable during the transient failure.
After recovery, the visitor still sees the board rather than an unavailable screen.

cases.title: Authorization expiry returns the visitor to password re-entry without a transient unavailable page
preconditions: The visitor initially has a ready password-admitted share.
Revalidation reports unavailable and the next bootstrap state is password-required.
setup: Open the ready board and advance to its early revalidation.
steps: Return an unavailable share-context response.
Return password-required from the recovery bootstrap.
assertions: The visitor is shown the password re-entry form after access expires.
The protected board is no longer visible.
The visitor does not remain on a misleading unavailable screen when re-authentication is available.

cases.title: Changed access or publication tuple replaces the viewer through recovery instead of mixing share revisions
preconditions: A ready board is visible.
A revalidation response differs in share, board, revision, publication generation, or access generation.
setup: Start a background revalidation while the existing board is displayed.
steps: Return the mismatched ready projection and allow the recovery bootstrap to complete.
assertions: The visitor sees one recovered public-share state, not a mix of the old board and a new authorization or publication generation.
If recovery cannot obtain a permitted state, the visitor sees the unavailable outcome with focus on its heading.

cases.title: Out-of-order revalidation responses cannot replace the current visitor state with stale content
preconditions: A ready board is visible and a revalidation request can be delayed.
setup: Trigger two refresh opportunities, making the first response arrive after the second request has become current.
steps: Resolve the current request to a valid state.
Then resolve the aborted or superseded request with a different state.
assertions: The visitor continues to see the board corresponding to the current request only.
A late response does not restore stale protected content or redirect the visitor away from the current visible outcome.

cases.title: Unsupported artifact isolation gives an accessible fallback rather than running public artifact content
preconditions: A published page contains an artifact node.
The browser reports that artifact isolation is unsupported.
setup: Open the public share in the unsupported browser condition.
steps: Allow artifact support detection to finish.
assertions: The visitor receives an alert-level browser-support fallback.
The isolated artifact runtime frame is not presented as usable content.

cases.title: Unavailable artifact package does not prevent the public board from giving a clear fallback
preconditions: A ready public share contains an artifact node but its store, runtime origin, or runtime summary is unavailable.
setup: Open the share and navigate to the page containing the artifact.
steps: Render the artifact node under the unavailable-artifact condition.
assertions: The visitor sees the artifact-unavailable alert in place of the artifact.
The surrounding shared-board reader remains intelligible rather than presenting a blank or stale artifact frame.

cases.title: Public visitor can run the pinned artifact and keep it intact while entering and leaving presentation
preconditions: A valid public-artifact URL serves a ready share with a pinned artifact package.
setup: Open the public artifact page in a browser where fullscreen permission is denied.
steps: Wait for the active artifact runtime frame and absence of the preparing fallback.
Open live presentation and start a new presentation.
Use pen, pointer, and eraser controls, then exit presentation.
assertions: The visitor sees the active pinned artifact rather than an execution-disabled or fallback message.
Presentation becomes active even when native fullscreen is denied.
The annotation toolbar is visible without overlapping the exit control, and the artifact frame remains the same visible runtime through annotation-tool changes.
After exit, the page visibly returns to non-presentation mode.

cases.title: Access-generation change disposes the prior public artifact route before showing renewed content
preconditions: A ready share has an open public artifact package store.
Recovery supplies a ready state with a changed access or publication generation.
setup: Display an artifact in the initial authorized state and trigger the changed-generation recovery.
steps: Allow recovery to replace the public-share state.
assertions: The visitor never continues to see the old artifact as the renewed share content.
The visible artifact outcome is either the renewed authorized artifact or its explicit unavailable fallback.

cases.title: Live-presentation dialog handles empty sessions, failure, dismissal, and keyboard focus accessibly
preconditions: A public visitor has a ready share and opens presentation controls.
setup: Return no active sessions, then make a refresh request fail.
steps: Open the live-presentation dialog.
Use Tab and Shift+Tab through its enabled controls.
Trigger refresh failure, then dismiss with Escape and reopen by clicking the backdrop.
assertions: The visitor sees the dialog title, start action, and no-active-sessions message.
Focus stays within the modal while it is open and returns to the previously focused control after dismissal.
A session-service failure is announced in the dialog without leaving a stuck busy state.

cases.title: Joining a live presentation makes a viewer follow the current page and blocks viewer editing/navigation
preconditions: The session list contains a live session whose fetched snapshot has role viewer and a current page different from the selected page.
setup: Open the session dialog on a multi-page ready share.
steps: Join the listed session.
Attempt page navigation and annotation input while the viewer session is active.
assertions: The visitor enters presentation and visibly follows the session's current page.
Viewer navigation is disabled and annotations are read-only, so the visitor cannot alter the presenter-controlled view.

cases.title: Presenter start, page change, and exit leave viewers with a coherent presentation outcome
preconditions: A ready multi-page public share can start a presentation session as presenter.
setup: Open presentation controls from a selected page.
steps: Start a new live presentation.
Move to another page while presenting.
Exit presentation.
assertions: Presentation visibly starts on the selected page.
The displayed page changes coherently during the presenter session.
On exit, presentation mode visibly turns off and the presenter is no longer left with a live presentation UI.

cases.title: Conflicting presenter annotation update recovers once with the latest session version
preconditions: A presenter has a live session and creates annotation strokes on the current page.
The first update returns HTTP 409 and the latest fetched session still grants presenter role.
setup: Produce a final annotation change after a concurrent session-version update.
steps: Return a 409 for the initial update.
Return the latest session snapshot, then accept the retried update using its version.
assertions: The presenter continues to see the presentation and the intended annotation rather than losing the presentation to a conflict.
The displayed page and annotation outcome remains coherent after the retry.

cases.title: Viewer event-stream recovery follows newer snapshots and exits cleanly when the session is deleted
preconditions: A visitor has joined a live session as viewer.
setup: Provide a newer presentation event, then a stale lower-version event.
Cause an EventSource error first recoverable by session fetch, then return HTTP 404 for a later recovery fetch.
steps: Deliver the newer and stale events.
Disconnect the event stream and resolve the recovery fetches as specified.
assertions: The viewer visibly follows the newer session page and does not move backward to stale presentation state.
After a recoverable disconnect, the presentation remains usable while the stream reconnects.
When the session is gone, presentation visibly exits and the reopened dialog reports that the live session ended.

cases.title: English presentation demo redirects only to its configured valid persistent share URL
preconditions: SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL_EN is a valid HTTPS URL on an allowed SceneBoard origin with an exact persistent share path.
setup: Use a valid English destination such as an allowed /s/share_<22-character-token>_g1 URL with no credentials, query, or fragment.
steps: Open /demo/presentation without a locale parameter.
assertions: The visitor is taken to the configured English persistent shared-presentation URL.

cases.title: Korean presentation demo chooses the Korean destination and falls back only to the generic Korean-compatible setting
preconditions: A valid generic presentation-demo URL is configured.
Run one state with a valid SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL_KO and one state without it.
setup: Configure distinct valid Korean and generic persistent-share URLs for the preference state.
steps: Open /demo/presentation?locale=ko with the Korean URL configured.
Open /demo/presentation?locale=ko after omitting the Korean-specific URL.
assertions: Korean visitors reach the Korean configured presentation when it exists, otherwise the configured generic persistent presentation.

cases.title: Missing, unsupported, and multi-value locales use the English presentation configuration
preconditions: SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL_EN is a valid allowed persistent-share URL.
setup: Prepare requests with no locale, an unsupported scalar locale, and a multi-value locale input.
steps: Open /demo/presentation for each prepared locale state.
assertions: Each visitor reaches the configured English persistent presentation rather than an ambiguous locale-specific destination.

cases.title: Absent or empty locale-resolved destination produces a visible not-found result
preconditions: For English, SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL_EN is absent or empty.
For Korean, both SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL_KO and SCENEBOARD_PRESENTATION_DEMO_URL are absent or empty.
setup: Run the English and Korean configuration states independently.
steps: Open /demo/presentation in the English state.
Open /demo/presentation?locale=ko in the Korean state.
assertions: The visitor sees the application's not-found outcome and is not sent to a presentation destination that is unavailable.

cases.title: Malformed and unsafe configured destinations are denied instead of redirecting the visitor
preconditions: Run destination values that are whitespace-padded, unparsable, non-HTTPS, outside the allowed origins, credential-bearing, query-bearing, fragment-bearing, or not an exact persistent-share path.
setup: Apply one invalid destination value at a time to the locale-resolved configuration.
steps: Open the corresponding /demo/presentation route for each invalid configuration.
assertions: The visitor sees the application's not-found outcome and is never redirected to the malformed or unapproved destination.

cases.title: Only exact persistent share identifiers and safe generations can become a presentation destination
preconditions: Use allowed-origin HTTPS URLs with a 22-character share token.
Include generation g1, a positive safe-integer generation, g0, a leading-zero generation, and a generation longer than the accepted 1-to-16 digit form.
setup: Keep all other URL components free of credentials, query, and fragment.
steps: Open /demo/presentation for each configured destination boundary value.
assertions: Visitors reach only destinations with an accepted persistent share identifier and generation; rejected identifier or generation values result in the visible not-found outcome.

cases.title: An unmodified primary touch activation selects current-tab sample navigation
preconditions: The presentation sample navigation caller supplies isPrimaryClick=true, hasModifierKey=false, and activationSource=touch.
setup: Invoke the shared navigation decision with the ordinary touch input.
steps: Activate the presentation sample through an unmodified primary touch interaction.
assertions: Inference: the caller may keep the visitor in the current tab for the ordinary touch presentation-sample journey.

cases.title: Keyboard, mouse, and modifier-key sample activations do not select the touch current-tab path
preconditions: Cover a keyboard activation, a mouse activation, and a touch activation with a modifier key.
setup: Invoke the shared navigation decision for each non-ordinary-touch input.
steps: Activate the presentation sample using each prepared interaction.
assertions: Inference: the caller does not force visitors using keyboard, mouse, or modifier-key activation onto the touch-only current-tab navigation path.

scenarios.entry_point: Root document shell and framework recovery routes

cases.title: Request locale renders a matching global document language
preconditions: A supported locale preference is available in the request locale cookie or Accept-Language header.
setup: Use a supported non-default locale such as ja in a browser request.
steps: Open a normal application page through the root layout.
Allow the initial document and localized global shell to render.
assertions: The rendered document language matches the resolved request locale.
[Inference from the included LocalizedSkipLink composition] A keyboard user can reach a skip-link affordance whose visible text matches that locale.

cases.title: Changing locale updates visible localization and the document language
preconditions: A rendered consumer of I18nProvider can request a supported replacement locale.
setup: Start a page with an initial locale different from the replacement locale.
steps: Trigger the application's locale-change path for a supported locale.
Observe localized content and the document after the update settles.
assertions: Visible localized copy is rendered using the newly selected locale.
The document language changes to the newly selected locale and the locale preference is retained for subsequent requests.

cases.title: Missing route presents a localized not-found recovery screen
preconditions: A supported locale is resolved for the request.
setup: Request an unmatched application route under a non-default locale.
steps: Wait for the framework not-found route to render.
Inspect the user-facing not-found content.
assertions: The user sees the localized not-found screen rather than an untranslated fallback.
For Russian, the displayed page-not-found copy is "Страница не найдена.".

cases.title: Localized global error can recover from a transient failure
preconditions: A recoverable rendering failure reaches the global error boundary.
The browser has a supported locale cookie.
setup: Cause one render attempt to fail and arrange for the retried attempt to succeed.
steps: Open the failing page and wait for the global error screen.
Activate the localized retry button once.
Wait for the retry outcome.
assertions: The user sees the localized "something went wrong" heading and localized retry control in the cookie-selected locale.
[Inference from the boundary reset callback] After the transient fault clears, the user returns to the retried page instead of remaining on an unusable error screen.

cases.title: Global error resolves locale from browser language when no cookie exists
preconditions: The browser has no locale cookie and reports a supported preferred language.
setup: Configure navigator languages to a supported non-default locale and trigger the global error boundary.
steps: Wait for client locale resolution after the error page mounts.
Inspect the error heading, retry control, and document language.
assertions: The error screen and document language match the locale resolved from browser languages rather than staying at the initial default locale.
If retry cannot clear the fault, the user remains on an understandable localized error screen with a usable retry control.

cases.title: Representative locale catalog copy remains user-visible and correct
preconditions: A test consumer renders messages through I18nProvider or formatMessage for supported locales.
setup: Render representative localized interface labels for ko, ja, and de.
steps: Render the landing hero base title in Korean.
Render the human-control navigation label in Japanese.
Render the HITL expand label in German.
assertions: Users see "Codex가 자유롭게 사용할 수 있는" for the Korean landing hero base title, "人によるコントロール" for Japanese human control, and "Erweitern" for German expand.

cases.title: Long localized landing headlines remain readable without altered copy
preconditions: The landing page is available in Korean, German, and Russian.
setup: Open the landing page in a narrow browser viewport for each locale.
steps: Inspect the primary hero heading and value-section heading for Korean, German, and Russian.
Navigate through the headings at the viewport boundary.
assertions: [Inference from locale-specific heading CSS] Each localized hero heading remains visible and readable without replacing its localized copy.
The value-section heading does not overflow its constrained readable width.

cases.title: Capability-change announcement is localized and politely announced
preconditions: A board capability-change event can be surfaced to a user in each supported locale.
setup: Open a board client and trigger a capability-change announcement.
steps: Observe the visible status announcement and its accessibility semantics.
Repeat for the supported locales named by the localization test.
assertions: Every affected user sees a non-empty localized capability-change message.
The announcement is exposed as a polite status update and does not disclose role names, policy labels, or internal board identifiers.

cases.title: Unauthenticated visitors are sent to sign-in before AI connection settings are shown
preconditions: The visitor has no authenticated route session.
steps: Open /settings/ai-connections.
assertions: The visitor lands on /login and cannot view AI connection, pairing, grant, or API-key content.

cases.title: An authenticated session loads independent pairing, grant, board, and API-key surfaces
preconditions: An authenticated route session is available.
setup: Provide successful active-pairing, grant, board, and API-key list responses.
steps: Open the AI connections settings screen.
assertions: The user sees the AI-client connection group and the separate API-key group with their returned data, rather than a mixed or missing connection method.

cases.title: API-key list gives a recoverable loading, empty, and refresh-error journey
preconditions: An authenticated session is bound to the API-key view.
setup: Exercise an empty successful list, a failed initial list, and a later successful retry.
steps: Open the API-key group; choose Retry after the failed load.
assertions: The user sees loading while data is requested, an empty-state message when no keys exist, and after retry sees the current key list instead of a permanently failed screen.

cases.title: A stale or invalidated account session scrubs the API-key view before recovery
preconditions: The API-key list has loaded, optionally with an issued secret dialog open.
setup: Cause the current session generation to become stale during list loading or through the generation invalidation subscription.
steps: Wait for the stale-session recovery path to reconcile the session.
assertions: No prior key, guide, or raw secret remains visible; the user is redirected to sign-in if signed out, otherwise is returned to a freshly reconciled settings view or an error state.

cases.title: API-key creation starts at minimum read authority and honors chosen scopes and duration
preconditions: The authenticated API-key list is ready.
steps: Open creation; inspect default scopes; choose a non-empty name, valid scopes, and 30, 90, or 365 days; submit.
assertions: The request reflects only selected scopes and the closed duration, with board:read selected by default rather than all authorities; success gives the issued-key setup dialog.

cases.title: API-key creation cannot issue a key with no authority
preconditions: The authenticated API-key list is ready.
steps: Choose Deselect all in the scope toolbar.
assertions: The Create API key control is disabled and no issued-key dialog or new list item appears.

cases.title: Optional blank names become usable timestamped names while entered names prevail
preconditions: The authenticated API-key list is ready.
setup: Run once with a whitespace-only name and once with a trimmed entered name.
steps: Submit a valid scoped creation request for each name variant.
assertions: The user sees a stable local timestamp-based name for blank input and the entered trimmed name for non-blank input; neither path presents a required-name validation error.

cases.title: Busy and stale create attempts do not leave an unintended API key or secret visible
preconditions: The API-key list is ready and creation is submitted.
setup: Delay the create response, attempt repeat activation while busy, then return either success under the same generation or stale_attempt.
steps: Attempt repeat submission while the form is busy; observe recovery after the response.
assertions: Inference: the busy control prevents a second user-visible issuance attempt; a matching success yields one new key and setup dialog, while a stale response recovers the session with no raw secret retained.

cases.title: API-key creation remains keyboard-operable and usable at compact widths
preconditions: The API-key creation form is open.
steps: Use keyboard focus and Space/Enter to select scopes; resize to 390px and 320px widths.
assertions: All scope controls and actions remain operable, interactive buttons meet the rendered 44px target, and the form has no horizontal overflow at 320px.

cases.title: A newly issued secret is shown once with a directly usable setup path
preconditions: A create response succeeds under the current session generation.
setup: Use a non-production test key value.
steps: Create a key and review the setup dialog's MCP and Environment tabs.
assertions: The user can copy the newly issued raw key and sees MCP JSON that includes it; both tab controls and panels are labelled and usable.

cases.title: Closing, navigating away from, or invalidating an issued-secret view prevents later raw-secret exposure
preconditions: A newly issued secret dialog is open.
steps: Attempt to close and reject confirmation, then confirm close; reopen the guide from the list and navigate away or trigger session invalidation.
assertions: Rejecting confirmation keeps the setup view available, but confirmed close, route change, unmount, or recovery removes the raw secret; reopening an existing key shows only its name and prefix with a secret-free environment reference.

cases.title: Setup-copy failures are announced without silently retaining or exporting the key
preconditions: A newly issued secret dialog is open and clipboard copying fails.
setup: Use a browser context that rejects clipboard copying.
steps: Activate the raw-secret copy control.
assertions: The user receives an accessible copy-failure alert and can still close the dialog; the screen does not offer a persistence, URL, analytics, or diagnostic export path for the secret.

cases.title: Pagination retains unique API-key entries and recovers from continuation failure
preconditions: The first page returns a next cursor.
setup: Return overlapping key metadata across pages; make one continuation request fail before retry or refresh succeeds.
steps: Choose Load more; then use Retry and Refresh after a continuation failure.
assertions: The user sees each API key only once, can recover a failed continuation, and receives a current coherent list after refresh.

cases.title: Revoke requires confirmation and reflects only the final mutation outcome
preconditions: At least one API-key metadata item is listed.
setup: Exercise confirmation cancellation, successful revocation, mutation failure, and stale_attempt.
steps: Choose Revoke, cancel confirmation once, then confirm it; repeat with failure and stale-session outcomes.
assertions: Cancellation leaves the key available, successful revocation removes only that key, and failure or stale session leaves no misleading success state and offers the applicable error or recovery outcome.

cases.title: Creating a pairing code persists only the active code and surfaces a newly pending request
preconditions: The owner is authenticated and no pairing mutation is active.
setup: Return a created pairing, then a pending owner status for the same pairing during a later refresh.
steps: Choose Create code and allow the visible-page refresh cycle to receive the pending request.
assertions: The owner sees the created one-time code while valid and the pending request opens for review when it arrives, rather than creating duplicate request cards.

cases.title: Pairing approval cannot grant capabilities above the owner ceiling
preconditions: A matching pending pairing request is selected.
setup: Request scopes and lifecycle permissions that include values outside the connection grant ceiling.
steps: Open the approval dialog and inspect selectable permissions before submitting.
assertions: The owner can approve only requested capabilities within the allowed ceiling; out-of-ceiling permissions are neither displayed as grants nor submitted as approval choices.

cases.title: Pairing approval validates scope and board destination before it can affect a board
preconditions: A matching pending pairing request is selected.
setup: Exercise no selected scope, no existing board, create destination without board.write and board.create, empty new-board title, and a valid existing-board destination.
steps: Try each destination and permission combination; then submit a valid existing-board choice.
assertions: Invalid selections display validation without approval; the valid choice proceeds with selected board, scopes, lifecycle permissions, and session or persistent lifetime.

cases.title: Approve, deny, and cancel produce distinct recoverable pairing outcomes
preconditions: A created or matching pending pairing exists.
setup: Return approval with one board ID, approval with another result shape, denial, cancellation, and an API failure.
steps: Perform each terminal action from the request dialog.
assertions: Approval takes the owner to its board when exactly one destination board is returned or to the boards index otherwise; denial and cancellation remove the local active code/request, while failure does not falsely navigate or approve.

cases.title: Pairing dialog is accessible and safely dismissible without accidental approval
preconditions: A pairing request dialog is open.
steps: Use the labelled close control, Escape, backdrop click, board search, radio group, and validation paths.
assertions: The dialog has an accessible title and description, dismissal closes it without approving or cancelling, board search reports no matches when appropriate, and validation errors are announced.

cases.title: Grant rotation and revocation leave the user with the current authorization state
preconditions: At least one approved client grant is listed.
setup: Exercise successful and failed rotate/revoke responses.
steps: Rotate a grant, dismiss the rotated credential, then revoke a grant.
assertions: A successful rotation presents the replacement credential only for its temporary view, and successful revocation removes the grant and updates visible connection state; failed operations do not claim either outcome.

cases.title: Authenticated user sees each listed board's visible lifecycle summary and can open it
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
The board list returns at least one active board and one archived board.
setup: Prepare board summaries with distinct titles, updated timestamps, head revision numbers, and archived states.
steps: Open /boards.
Wait for the initial board-list request to resolve.
Activate an active board card.
assertions: The loading placeholder is replaced by board cards showing each title, revision, formatted update time, and the active or archived lifecycle label.
The selected board opens at its encoded /boards/{boardId} URL.

cases.title: Authenticated user receives the empty-board outcome with an accessible creation control
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
The board list resolves successfully with no boards.
setup: Return an empty board page with no next cursor.
steps: Open /boards after the initial list completes.
Navigate to the board-title field and Create control with assistive technology.
assertions: The page presents the no-boards empty-state message instead of board cards.
The board-title field has its visible label, is required, and the Create control remains reachable and named for the user.

cases.title: User loads the next board page without losing the boards already visible
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
The first board-list response has a non-null next cursor.
setup: Return a first page and a distinct subsequent page for the supplied cursor.
steps: Open /boards and wait for the first page.
Choose Load more.
Wait for the cursor request to complete.
assertions: The control communicates loading and cannot be invoked again while the next page is loading.
After completion, the user sees the original boards together with the additional boards, rather than a replaced or duplicated first page.

cases.title: Forbidden board-list response is surfaced as an accessible authorization denial and can be retried
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
The initial board-list request returns the FORBIDDEN board error.
setup: Make the retry list request resolve successfully after the denial.
steps: Open /boards.
Locate the error alert.
Choose Retry list.
assertions: The user receives the localized forbidden outcome in an alert rather than a misleading successful board list.
After retry succeeds, the alert clears and the user sees the returned board-list outcome.

cases.title: List transport, malformed-response, and unsupported-browser failures give a recoverable user-visible outcome
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
setup: Independently return api failure, corrupt response, and unsupported-browser results from the list request; make a retry resolve successfully.
steps: Open /boards for each failure result.
Read the alert and choose Retry list.
Wait for the retry response.
assertions: Each failure presents its mapped user-visible error in an alert, including the distinct corrupt-response and unsupported-browser outcomes where supplied.
A successful retry restores a usable board-list or empty-state outcome.

cases.title: Authenticated user creates a board from a trimmed valid title, including the 200-character boundary
preconditions: An authenticated session with a CSRF token is available.
setup: Prepare a successful create response with a board ID containing characters that require URL encoding.
Use a title whose trimmed value is exactly 200 characters.
steps: Open /boards.
Enter surrounding whitespace and the boundary-length title.
Submit Create.
assertions: The field enforces the 200-character limit and is visibly unavailable while creation is pending.
After a successful create, the user reaches the newly created board at its encoded detail URL.

cases.title: Creation recovers from a retryable failure without changing the request identity for the same title
preconditions: An authenticated session with a CSRF token is available.
setup: Return a corrupt-response or unsupported-browser create failure on the first submit, then a successful create response when the unchanged title is resubmitted.
[Inference] The backend honors the unchanged client request identity to avoid a duplicate creation.
steps: Enter a non-empty title and submit Create.
Observe the error outcome.
Submit the unchanged title again.
assertions: The first failure leaves the user on the boards page with a user-visible error and an enabled creation control.
The successful retry takes the user to one newly created board rather than exposing a duplicate-creation outcome.

cases.title: Create authorization or API rejection does not navigate away and permits a corrected retry
preconditions: An authenticated session with a CSRF token is available.
setup: Return a board_error or api_error from creation, then a successful response on a subsequent submit.
steps: Enter a valid title and submit Create.
Observe the rejection outcome.
Submit again after the service accepts the request.
assertions: The rejected creation keeps the user on /boards with the mapped user-visible error, rather than navigating to an uncreated board.
After a later successful submission, the user reaches the created board detail page.

cases.title: A board created after the /boards polling baseline automatically opens from the list
preconditions: The authenticated user is on visible /boards.
The initial lifecycle poll establishes a board-ID baseline.
setup: Return a subsequent successful list response containing one new board.
steps: Remain on /boards until the subsequent lifecycle poll completes.
assertions: The user is taken to the newly detected board's encoded detail URL.
The initial baseline itself does not unexpectedly move the user away from /boards.

cases.title: A newly created board automatically opens while the user is on AI connections
preconditions: The authenticated user is on visible /settings/ai-connections.
The initial lifecycle poll establishes a board-ID baseline.
setup: Return a later successful list response with one board not in the baseline.
steps: Remain on AI connections until the lifecycle poll detects the new board.
assertions: The user transitions from AI connections to the newly detected board's encoded detail URL.

cases.title: User viewing a board can explicitly switch to a newly detected board
preconditions: The authenticated user is on /boards/{currentBoardId}.
A polling baseline has been established.
setup: Return a later board-list response containing a new board with a visible title.
steps: Wait for the new-board confirmation dialog.
Choose Switch to new board.
assertions: The confirmation identifies the detected board by title and has explicit switch and keep actions.
After confirmation, the user reaches the new board's encoded detail URL.

cases.title: User viewing a board can dismiss new-board detection and keep the current context
preconditions: The authenticated user is on /boards/{currentBoardId}.
A later lifecycle poll finds another board.
setup: Return the current board normally and return a board-list response containing one new board.
steps: Wait for the new-board confirmation dialog.
Choose Keep current board.
assertions: The dialog closes after dismissal.
The user remains on the current board detail route rather than being redirected to the new board.

cases.title: Archived or missing current board returns the user to the boards index
preconditions: The authenticated user is on /boards/{boardId}.
setup: Independently return an archived board, BOARD_NOT_FOUND, and API 404 from the current-board read.
steps: Wait for the lifecycle check for each terminal board state.
assertions: For each explicit archived or not-found outcome, the user is returned to /boards instead of being left on an invalid board detail route.

cases.title: Transient or ambiguous current-board errors do not evict the user from a still-current board
preconditions: The authenticated user is on /boards/{boardId}.
setup: Independently return API 503, reconciliation_required, and corrupt_response from the current-board read.
steps: Wait for a lifecycle check for each non-terminal result.
assertions: The user remains on the current board detail route for transient or ambiguous results, avoiding a destructive redirect based on an unconfirmed terminal state.

cases.title: Concurrent external board creations select the newest board with a stable tie break
preconditions: The authenticated user is on visible /boards or AI connections after its baseline is established.
setup: Return several boards absent from the baseline, including two with equal newest createdAt values and board IDs that establish the documented stable selection order.
steps: Allow the next lifecycle list poll to complete.
assertions: The user reaches the deterministic newest selected board detail route, preserving a predictable outcome when multiple boards appear in one poll.

cases.title: Hidden-tab polling does not interrupt the user and resumes lifecycle detection when visible
preconditions: The authenticated user is on a lifecycle-watched route and a baseline has been established.
setup: Make a new board appear while document visibility is hidden, then expose the document.
steps: Hide the browser tab while the board is created.
Restore tab visibility.
assertions: No lifecycle navigation occurs while the tab is hidden.
Once visible, the user receives the route's appropriate new-board outcome: automatic detail navigation on creation-auto-open routes or a confirmation dialog on a board detail route.

cases.title: Boards page shell supplies a named primary navigation and an accessible page name
preconditions: An authenticated session is available.
setup: Render /boards through its authenticated page wrapper and AppShell.
steps: Open /boards.
Inspect landmarks and navigate with a screen reader or keyboard.
assertions: The page provides a named primary navigation with Boards and AI connections destinations.
The main landmark contains the localized boards page name and the board workspace content is reachable without relying on visual-only structure.

cases.title: Board loading, retryable failure, and successful retry have visible route outcomes
preconditions: A signed-in user can open a board URL.
setup: Arrange a pending board session, then a retryable failure, then a successful retry response.
steps: Open the board URL.
Observe the pending route.
Use Retry after the failure.
Allow the next request to succeed.
assertions: The user sees a loading status while the board is pending.
Failure shows a retry path rather than a usable-looking stale canvas.
Successful retry shows the board workspace and selected page.

cases.title: An unresolved or unrenderable selected page fails closed
preconditions: A signed-in user opens a board with no resolvable selected page or a page-render adaptation failure.
setup: Supply the invalid board response.
steps: Open the board URL.
assertions: The user sees the scene-unavailable outcome.
The route does not display partial or stale page content as usable.

cases.title: Admitted keyboard navigation changes the page and announces the new position
preconditions: A live board has at least two pages and no text input, artifact capture, HITL interaction, or page-move capture is active.
setup: Open the first page.
steps: Use an admitted keyboard navigation command.
Return with the previous-page control or command.
assertions: Each command visibly shows the adjacent requested page.
The new page starts at the top and announces its current position.

cases.title: Desktop and mobile keep one reachable vertical page surface
preconditions: A board page has terminal scene content taller than the viewport.
setup: Open the same board at desktop width and at a width no greater than 760px.
steps: Scroll to final rendered content on both viewports.
Reach page controls by keyboard.
assertions: Final scene content is visible and reachable on both viewports.
The user does not encounter horizontal document overflow or clipped nested scrolling.
The canvas remains a labeled keyboard-focusable region.

cases.title: Page-move gestures preserve interactive controls and recover after cancellation
preconditions: A canvas page is wider than its viewport and page-move mode is available.
setup: Enable page-move and expose a button, form control, or HITL/artifact capture target.
steps: Start a pointer gesture on an interactive target.
Pan non-interactive content horizontally.
Cancel through capture loss, window blur, or orientation change.
assertions: Interactive targets remain usable rather than being panned.
Non-interactive content can pan when enabled.
Cancellation leaves the page in a usable bounded position.

cases.title: An authorized user selects retained history and returns to latest accessibly
preconditions: The user has board.history.read and the board has retained revisions.
setup: Open desktop history combobox and mobile history sidebar.
steps: Open with Enter, Space, or arrow key.
Choose a retained revision with listbox keyboard controls.
Choose Latest.
assertions: The selected revision is visibly marked and displayed.
Latest returns the user to the live board.
Expanded and active-option states are exposed to assistive technology.

cases.title: History communicates loading, empty, and additional-page states
preconditions: The user has board.history.read.
setup: Prepare loading, empty-ready, and next-cursor history responses.
steps: Open history during loading.
Observe empty retained history.
Choose Load more or press PageDown when a next cursor exists.
assertions: The user is told history is loading.
An empty retained list does not hide Latest.
Additional revisions become available without making prior choices unavailable.

cases.title: History failure and unavailable selection provide a recoverable visible result
preconditions: The user has board.history.read.
setup: Make history fail then retry successfully; separately make a selected retained revision unavailable.
steps: Open history and cause failure.
Choose Retry.
Attempt the unavailable selection and return to Latest.
assertions: The user sees unavailable history with Retry.
Retry restores usable history or Latest.
The user receives an unavailable-selection message instead of silently viewing stale history and retains usable focus.

cases.title: A viewer sees only current board reading and cannot reach privileged workflows
preconditions: The user receives only board.read capability.
setup: Open the board at desktop and mobile widths.
steps: Inspect identity, revision controls, utility rail, and drawer.
Attempt ordinary keyboard navigation to restricted actions.
assertions: Current board content is visible.
Edit, history, connection, presentation, export, sharing, membership, analytics, archive, and deletion controls are not offered.
Keyboard navigation does not reveal a usable restricted action.

cases.title: An editor gets literal granted workflows but no owner workflows
preconditions: The user has evidence-backed editor capabilities including board.write, history, media, HITL, artifact control, and own-connection management, but no owner administration capabilities.
setup: Open the board as editor.
steps: Use rename, history, and connection entry points.
Inspect owner administration and presentation controls.
assertions: Granted edit, history, and own-connection workflows are available.
Sharing, membership, analytics, export, archive, deletion, and presentation controls are not offered.
Visible outcomes follow literal capabilities, not an inferred role name.

cases.title: A fully authorized owner can reach administration workflows and dismiss board controls safely
preconditions: The user has the evidence-backed owner capabilities and board.archive lifecycle permission.
setup: Open owner actions from desktop rail and mobile drawer.
steps: Reach sharing, membership, analytics, export, settings, and archive.
Open board controls and dismiss with close, Escape, and backdrop pointer.
assertions: Every owner workflow is reachable.
Board controls expose expanded state and a labeled dialog.
Each dismissal returns the user to a usable board.

cases.title: Loss of a capability closes privileged UI, exits unsafe state, and restores focus
preconditions: An owner or editor has an open privileged workflow when its server-provided capability epoch removes that permission.
setup: Open history, owner controls, or presentation controls before the reduced capability state arrives.
steps: Deliver the reduced capability state.
Try to continue with the retained prior control.
assertions: The privileged surface closes and is no longer offered.
History loss returns the user to current live content and presentation-management loss exits presentation.
A capabilities-changed announcement occurs and focus reaches a connected drawer trigger or page canvas.

cases.title: Confirmed archive redirects only after one successful archive outcome
preconditions: The user has full owner administration capabilities.
setup: Arrange an archive response that can be delayed, aborted, or succeed.
steps: Cancel archive confirmation.
Submit it once and rapidly repeat submission while pending.
Allow the request to succeed.
assertions: Cancellation leaves the usable existing board.
The board list is not shown before success.
After success, the user is redirected to /boards once and cannot continue using archived board owner controls.

cases.title: Aborted or failed archive preserves a safe recoverable board state
preconditions: The owner opened archive confirmation.
setup: Abort the in-flight archive request or return failure.
steps: Submit archive and trigger the failure.
Dismiss the failed flow and continue interacting.
assertions: The user remains on the existing board rather than being redirected as if archive succeeded.
The owner can continue from a usable board state.

cases.title: An authorized owner starts or joins presentation and recovers when fullscreen is denied
preconditions: The owner has share.manage and a board revision with a selected page.
setup: Make session listing available and make requestFullscreen reject with NotAllowedError.
steps: Choose Present, then select an existing session or start one.
Navigate the presentation top bar by keyboard.
Press Escape or choose Exit presentation.
assertions: The user enters a focused presentation view with one presentation top bar despite fullscreen denial.
A keyboard-reachable control remains in the viewport.
Exit returns to ordinary top bar with usable focus.

cases.title: A viewer follows newer presentation state but cannot navigate independently
preconditions: A live presentation exists and the joining user is a viewer.
setup: Join as viewer, then advance presenter to another page.
steps: Try viewer page navigation.
Deliver a newer session event.
Inference from evidence: interrupt the stream and let the recovery fetch return the latest state.
assertions: Viewer navigation is disabled.
The viewer visibly follows the presenter page.
After the inferred interruption, the viewer converges on the latest page and does not regress to an older one.

cases.title: Rapid presenter updates converge on the newest shared annotation and page
preconditions: A presenter and viewer share a live presentation.
setup: Make one presentation update return 409, then accept the retry after refreshed version retrieval.
steps: Make rapid annotation and page updates.
Deliver the conflict and refreshed session.
Observe the settled viewer state.
assertions: The presenter remains in a usable session after conflict.
The viewer sees the newest page and final annotations rather than an older conflicting version.

cases.title: Open unplaced HITL decisions are discoverable and escape collapses expanded view
preconditions: A live board has open HITL requests not placed in the rendered scene.
setup: Open a board whose decision-workspace policy prefers expanded view.
steps: Locate the decision workspace.
Toggle expanded view.
Press Escape while expanded.
assertions: Every unplaced open decision is visible in the named workspace.
The toggle exposes pressed state.
Escape returns to standard view without losing decision review access.

cases.title: Historical and non-writing views do not complete live HITL decisions
preconditions: The user is viewing history or lacks board.write.
setup: Open a board containing HITL content.
steps: Locate the HITL block and attempt normal decision interaction.
assertions: The user can review displayed interaction context.
The user-visible HITL control remains non-live and does not complete a live decision from this view.

cases.title: Public Codex installation page presents the onboarding entry point and reaches installation instructions
preconditions: Open the public /integrations/codex route.
steps: Load /integrations/codex.
Activate the hero action that links to the installation section.
assertions: The document title is 'Install SceneBoard for Codex'.
The page visibly presents its localized Codex onboarding title and description, a launch-status notice, and the numbered installation sections.
The action moves the user to the visible installation section rather than leaving them at an unrelated route.

cases.title: Codex plugin archive download produces the advertised archive for the user
preconditions: Open the public /integrations/codex route in a browser that permits downloads.
steps: Select the archive-download action in the hero.
assertions: The browser starts a download from /downloads/sceneboard-codex-plugin.zip with the suggested filename sceneboard-codex-plugin.zip.
The downloaded file is a ZIP archive, giving the user a usable plugin archive rather than an error document.

cases.title: Origin-aware install-guide URL is copied with temporary user feedback
preconditions: Open /integrations/codex in a browser with clipboard write permission.
steps: Wait for the client page to finish hydrating.
Use the copy control beside the install-guide URL.
assertions: The displayed guide URL is the value resolved for the current browser origin after hydration.
The copied clipboard value equals the guide URL displayed to the user.
The control visibly changes to the localized copied confirmation and returns to its localized copy label after approximately two seconds.

cases.title: Install, update, and removal instructions expose the required Codex commands for copying
preconditions: Open /integrations/codex in a browser with clipboard write permission.
steps: Review the command block in installation step 02.
Review the update and removal command blocks in maintenance step 05.
Copy each command block.
assertions: The installation block visibly contains 'codex plugin marketplace add leecatinc/sceneboard' followed by 'codex plugin add sceneboard@sceneboard'.
The maintenance blocks visibly contain the marketplace upgrade plus plugin-add command and 'codex plugin remove sceneboard@sceneboard'.
Each copy action places its complete displayed command block on the clipboard and gives the user copied feedback.

cases.title: Clipboard denial does not show a false success and a later retry recovers
preconditions: Open /integrations/codex with control over the browser clipboard permission.
steps: Deny clipboard write permission and select a copy control.
Grant clipboard write permission and select the same copy control again.
assertions: After the denied attempt, the control remains at its localized copy label instead of reporting copied success.
After permission is restored, the retry copies the displayed value and visibly reports copied success.

cases.title: Codex configuration priorities and authorization entry point are visible to the installer
preconditions: Open the public /integrations/codex route.
steps: Review configuration step 03.
Activate the authorization action in step 04.
assertions: The configuration priority list visibly presents the project .mcp.json override, the Codex configuration path, and https://sceneboard.dev as the production default in that order.
The authorization action directs the browser to /settings/ai-connections, giving the installer the configured connection-management entry point.

cases.title: Brand, sign-in, and language controls navigate the public installer without concealing primary navigation
preconditions: Open the public /integrations/codex route.
steps: Activate the brand link.
Return to /integrations/codex and activate the sign-in link.
Return again and operate the language selector.
assertions: The brand link takes the user to /boards and the sign-in link takes the user to /login.
The primary navigation remains available while the language selector is operable, so the user retains access to navigation and localized installer content.

cases.title: Codex onboarding has an accessible main landmark and usable primary navigation
preconditions: Open /integrations/codex with an accessibility tree or assistive technology.
steps: Navigate by landmarks and headings.
Inspect the primary navigation and the decorative logo card in the accessibility tree.
assertions: Assistive technology exposes a primary navigation landmark with its localized label and a main landmark containing the page's localized level-one title and installation sections.
The decorative logo card is omitted from the accessibility tree, while actionable links and copy controls remain reachable by their visible localized names.

cases.title: Valid authorized export session renders the first presentation page after resources are ready
preconditions: A session ID has exactly 22 URL-safe base64url characters.
The export API and artifact runtime origins are exact HTTP loopback origins.
The projection response is HTTP 200 with application/vnd.sceneboard.export-projection+json and a valid V1 document.
setup: Provide a one-or-more-page projection with a matching format descriptor and session-scoped resource URLs.
Provide the CSP-authorized Korean and Latin Noto Sans KR font resources required for readiness.
steps: Open the internal export-render route with the valid session ID.
Wait until the first page's fonts and export-ready content have settled.
assertions: The first presentation page is visibly rendered at the projection's declared dimensions rather than remaining an empty busy region.
The rendered export does not rely on browser storage or cookies.

cases.title: Authorized renderer selects a requested in-range page and rejects an out-of-range selection
preconditions: A valid authorized export session has loaded a projection containing at least two pages.
The renderer readiness bridge is available only after projection validation succeeds.
setup: Use a projection with visibly distinct first and second pages and all required resources.
steps: Request rendering of the second page through the export renderer bridge.
Request rendering with a negative index and an index equal to the page count.
assertions: The requested in-range presentation page becomes visibly rendered and ready before the request resolves successfully.
Invalid page selections do not replace the visible authorized page with unintended content.

cases.title: Invalid session identifiers and non-loopback configuration do not expose an export render surface
preconditions: The route accepts only a 22-character URL-safe session ID.
Configured API and artifact runtime origins must be origin-only HTTP loopback URLs without a path, query, or fragment.
setup: Prepare malformed session IDs and configuration candidates using localhost, HTTPS, non-loopback hosts, paths, queries, and fragments.
steps: Request the route with each malformed session ID.
Request a syntactically valid route under each invalid origin configuration.
assertions: An invalid session route presents no export content.
A configuration that could send the renderer to a non-loopback or rewritten origin presents no usable export render surface.

cases.title: Malformed, oversized, redirected, or contract-mismatched projections never render supplied content
preconditions: Projection fetches use no-store caching and redirect:error.
Accepted projection bytes must be between 1 and 1048576 bytes and decode as UTF-8 JSON.
The projection, format descriptor, resources, usage identities, SHA-256 values, media types, and session-scoped resource URLs are all strictly validated.
setup: Prepare one otherwise valid response for each failure boundary: empty body, 1048577-byte body, wrong media type, redirect, malformed JSON, wrong document/format, and an invalid resource identity or URL.
steps: Open the authorized render route for each invalid projection response.
assertions: No board page or attacker-supplied resource becomes visible for any rejected projection.
The page does not convert an invalid projection into a partially rendered export.

cases.title: Export document policy confines an authorized renderer to approved loopback endpoints
preconditions: The internal renderer is served with its dedicated document policy and a valid nonce.
The requester reaches the internal route as a loopback peer carrying its export bearer.
setup: Attempt frame, connection, worker, and stylesheet injection from non-approved origins while rendering a valid session.
steps: Open the authorized renderer and attempt the disallowed resource loads.
Attempt the same route without its bearer or from a non-loopback peer.
assertions: The authorized export page remains visible only within its intended renderer and does not display injected remote, worker, or framed content.
Unauthorized requests do not show export content.

cases.title: Revision-pinned PDF and PPTX exports publish only complete downloadable files
preconditions: An owner export request supplies a board ID, exact revision ID, CSRF token, and either pdf or pptx format.
The export response has the matching success content type, a safe attachment filename, matching content length, no-store/private cache controls, and nosniff.
setup: Prepare complete PDF and PPTX byte responses for the same named revision.
steps: Request a PDF export and a PPTX export for the pinned revision.
Publish each admitted result through the download publisher.
assertions: For each requested format, the user receives one downloadable file with the safe revision-specific filename and matching document type.
Each temporary download URL is revoked after the download is triggered.

cases.title: Failed, cancelled, redirected, partial, and contradictory export responses never become downloads
preconditions: The export client has a 120-second deadline and accepts caller cancellation.
The failure contract defines retryability for server failure codes.
setup: Prepare a timeout, caller cancellation, redirected response, opaque redirect, wrong content length, mismatched bytes, unsafe filename, malformed error, and contradictory retryability response.
steps: Start an export under each failure condition.
For a retryable server failure, perform a later fresh export attempt with a complete valid response.
assertions: No failed, cancelled, redirected, partial, or contradictory response produces a downloadable file.
Inference: after a retryable failure, a later complete response can provide the requested download without treating the failed response as a file.

cases.title: Concurrent revision-pinned export requests keep each user's downloadable result isolated
preconditions: Inference: concurrent export initiation is a relevant high-risk boundary because the client carries a board ID and a revision ID in every request.
Two valid requests use the same board with different revision IDs and formats.
setup: Arrange complete valid responses whose names, bytes, and content types visibly distinguish the two requested revisions.
steps: Start both export requests before either response settles.
Allow the responses to settle in reverse order.
assertions: Inference: each user receives only the complete file matching that user's requested revision and format, with no cross-request file substitution.
No response is published twice as a download.

cases.title: Anonymous visitor completes email verification and creates an account
preconditions: The session reconciliation result is anonymous.
A disposable email address can receive the six-digit verification code.
setup: Open /signup with no existing authenticated session.
steps: Enter a valid email address and request a verification code.
Enter the received six-digit code and submit verification.
Enter a password of at least 10 characters and submit account creation.
assertions: The page announces that the email is verified before password entry is available.
The user is redirected to /settings/ai-connections after successful account creation.

cases.title: Existing authenticated session bypasses signup and reaches AI connection settings
preconditions: Session reconciliation returns an existing authenticated session.
setup: Navigate directly to /signup while authenticated.
steps: Wait for initial session reconciliation.
assertions: The user is redirected to /settings/ai-connections instead of being able to create another account.

cases.title: Code sending resists rapid repeat activation and exposes the resend cooldown
preconditions: The visitor is anonymous and the email field contains a value.
setup: Open /signup.
steps: Activate Send code repeatedly while the first request is pending, then observe the completed state.
Attempt to activate resend before the displayed cooldown has elapsed.
assertions: The user sees one code-entry step and a disabled resend control with the countdown instead of repeated sends.
The control becomes available only after the displayed resend delay reaches zero.

cases.title: Invalid six-digit verification code keeps the visitor in a recoverable verification state
preconditions: A verification code has been sent for the entered email address.
setup: Open the code-entry step on /signup.
steps: Submit an invalid six-digit code.
assertions: An invalid-verification-code alert is visible.
The code-entry step remains available so the visitor can try another code.

cases.title: Rate-limited verification request exposes retry timing without trusting API error text
preconditions: The visitor is anonymous and a verification request receives RATE_LIMITED with a retry-after value.
setup: Enter an email address on /signup.
steps: Request a verification code while the rate limit response is returned.
assertions: The user sees the localized rate-limit outcome with the retry delay.
The raw API error message is not shown to the user.

cases.title: Malformed verification API payload fails safely in the signup journey
preconditions: Inference: the client maps a rejected exact-shape verification payload to its ordinary failure result.
The verification response omits a required field, has an unexpected field, or uses non-positive timing values.
setup: Open the relevant signup code-request or verification step.
steps: Cause the malformed verification response to be received.
assertions: The user sees the generic verification-failed outcome rather than advancing to password entry or seeing malformed response content.

cases.title: Expired verification ticket returns the visitor to the email-verification recovery path
preconditions: The visitor has verified an email and reached password entry.
The signup request returns verification_required.
setup: Enter a password on the verified-email step.
steps: Submit account creation after the verification ticket is no longer accepted.
assertions: The password-entry step is removed and the user sees the expired-verification message.
The user can request a new verification code for the retained email address.

cases.title: Email already in use remains a visible signup outcome
preconditions: The visitor has a valid verification ticket for an email already associated with an account.
setup: Reach the password-entry step on /signup.
steps: Submit a password to create the account.
assertions: The user remains on signup and sees the email-in-use alert rather than a success redirect.

cases.title: Signup preserves native field constraints and exposes state changes accessibly
preconditions: The visitor is anonymous.
setup: Open /signup using keyboard and assistive technology.
steps: Navigate to the email, verification-code, and password steps.
Attempt to submit a password shorter than 10 characters after successful verification.
assertions: Each visible input has its associated label and the verification code accepts exactly six numeric characters.
The verified-email status and error outcomes are announced, and native validation prevents account creation with the short password.

cases.title: Session reconciliation failure blocks unsafe signup submission with a visible error
preconditions: Session reconciliation returns an error.
setup: Navigate to /signup.
steps: Wait for session reconciliation to fail.
assertions: The user sees the session-failed alert and the signup controls remain disabled instead of submitting without a resolved session state.
